svg.aria-label: Three columns. Left: the Rust source, a device function that stores a value and then loops forever, and the kernel line that calls it. Middle: what the compiler emitted before, the call replaced by a device trap, so the store was lost. Right: what it emits now, the call followed by unreachable, so the PTX stores the value and spins; a small box lists the three cases that still trap.

text.style: font: 600 17px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: A device function that never returns is now called, not replaced by a trap

text.style: font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: Such a function may store an error code and then loop. The importer replaced the call with trap; and lost the store. Now it emits the call, then unreachable, as rustc's own backend does.

text.style: font: 600 11px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre
font: 600 11px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: BEFORE, ON MAIN (the call became a trap)

svg.text: callee's type promises it does not return.

svg.text: How the importer decides (translate_call, for a MIR Call with no return edge)

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: run_pipeline records the mangled name of every function it emits for this build. translate_call resolves the callee and checks that set:

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: in the set: emit the call, then unreachable, which is what rustc's own LLVM backend emits for a call with no destination.

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: not in the set: trap; then unreachable, as before. That blanket trap was written for panic entry points, which have no body on the GPU; it swallowed user functions as well.
